What are clients waiting for ? Im testing CLs with 64 validators, but even after 2 more epochs ,the cgc value is still just shows 0x04 Finalized beacon state any reason cgc value is not set pre fulu? I don't get it why you would need finalized beacon state It’s in spec There was some reason related to inactivity leak still dont' get it why can't it be set ahead of time? This means during fulu fork transition, there will be no supernodes for 2 epochs 😮 Not really the ones who use the flag will advertise as a supernode Tho yes i agree the percentage will be lesser Regarding Prysm it's a known bug. The correct `cgc` should be advertised regardless the fork we are in (before or after fulu). Currently, Prysm advertises the correct `cgc` only at Fulu. We are fixing this bug while implementing the latest validator custody spec (the one of this week). nobody will manually set it as a flag to be a supernode at least I won't count on anyone doing so right now I'm only testing lighthouse and lodestar, and neither of them advertising the right cgc even 2 epochs after fulu (as the chain is unfinalized) I think using this flag should adopt same behavior than managing 4096 ETH. Among other, once this flag is set, unsetting it won't have any effect. (`cgc` won't decrease) even after the chain has finalized, both lodestar and lighthouse report 0x04 for cgc so there is def some bug in client implementations here <@554799849288105986> <@1035747431461167125> ^ probably I'd really like it if all clients advertised their cgc pre fulu already, like Manu said prysm is planning to do this is going to help avoid possibly huge loads during fork transition <@412614104222531604> is that a mistake? ```yaml network_params: fulu_fork_epoch: 1 bpo_1_epoch: 2 bpo_1_max_blobs: 12 bpo_1_target_blobs: 9d ``` (last line) In https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/fusaka-devnet-1 yes fixed Currently, when the cgc increases, Prysm tries to subscribe to new subnets and find peers in these subnets. Only when peers are found, Prysm considers corresponding new data columns as needed to declare the block as available. After reflexion, I think it kind of defeat the purpose of validator custody, because is no peers are never found in the new subnets, then these new columns won't never be needed to declare the block as available. I also understand that, when new validators are added, the node needs some time to subscribe to new subnets and find peers in these subnets (if not already the case). So, when new validators are added, requiring immediately to receive new columns to declare the block as available may be too hard. Question to clients: What do you currently implement in such a case? New columns are immediately required? New columns are required after a reasonable delay? New columns are required when enough peers are found? Other? > So, when new validators are added, requiring immediately to receive new columns to declare the block as available may be too hard. i recall raising something exactly like this a few weeks ago https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1369325353243512905/1374043097255772240 my strategy is to not subscribe to any new subnet if we are within 2 seconds into the slot which is why the DA should just be static, circling back on it once again. either make it samples per slot or number of columns cc <@520034910149410861> <@592004585506340885> we do set, but we don't have a fusaka 1 branch yet double checked, we set it right at start up I don't think the DA should be static, clients can handle the increase however they like in my opinion, in terms of data availability requirements for attesting. For example, it would definitely not make sense to require new columns for attesting if the validators have been added 3.9s into the slot Fixed delay or waiting until enough peers are found (some indicator of "joining new subnets is completed") both seem reasonable, don't think it should be specced though At the risk of overloading the epoch transition, why not just modify DA at new epochs? That reduces some of these cases right? Are there test cases that produce different results for EIP- 7951 vs RIP-7212 ? Or properly implemented eip-7212 fully matches eip-7951? <@550420431744794624> mentioned that there were 700+ tests already, I’d assume those were all made for 7212.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Currently, when the cgc increases, Prysm tries to subscribe to new subnets and find peers in these subnets.
Only when peers are found, Prysm considers corresponding new data columns as needed to declare the block as available.
After reflexion, I think it kind of defeat the purpose of validator custody, because is no peers are never found in the new subnets, then these new columns won't never be needed to declare the block as available.

I also understand that, when new validators are added, the node needs some time to subscribe to new subnets and find peers in these subnets (if not already the case). So, when new validators are added, requiring immediately to receive new columns to declare the block as available may be too hard.

Question to clients: What do you currently implement in such a case?
New columns are immediately required? New columns are required after a reasonable delay? New columns are required when enough peers are found? Other?
